narrative.overview:
Each scenario is an exhibit laid on a table under good light. The employee inspects it, decides, and then sees exactly where the red flags were: numbered yellow tent markers drop onto the screenshot itself, and an evidence log beside it says what each one shows. The admin sees the same markers toned by how often the workforce missed them. Everything in the system serves that inspection: a graphite frame that recedes, a cool concrete ground, white work surfaces, and colour held back until it means something.

The density is operational, not promotional. These are work surfaces for refinery staff on phones and shared desktops and for a security team at office desktops: hairlines instead of shadowed cards, 1 to 2px corners, one sans family whose weights carry the hierarchy, and a mono for anything that has to be read character by character. Motion is spent on the reveal, where it carries the lesson; everywhere else a state change is a 150ms colour shift.

The world refuses the category default for quiz apps: a centred quiz card with a percentage progress bar, confetti and a blue SaaS shell. It also refuses decoration: no gradients, no glass panels, no side-stripe callouts, no kicker labels above headings.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite shell, concrete ground, white work surfaces.
Marker yellow is reserved for the one primary action, the current selection and the evidence markers.
Manila is paper: codes, exhibit tags and notes you carry with you.
Red and green mean outcome state only, and travel with a glyph and a word.
Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for everything; Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for codes, IDs and addresses.
1 to 2px corners, 1px hairlines, exactly two shadows.
The tent marker and the exhibit tag are the signature devices.

rules.name: The Marker Rule
rules.body: Marker yellow means act here, you are here, or look here. One yellow button per view; everything else that moves the user on is graphite. It is never a panel background, never decoration, and never text on a light surface, where it falls to 1.7:1.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: Manila is the paper in the evidence room: tags, code chips, the resume-code slip, the next clue, caution notes. It labels and informs; it is never a button.

rules.name: The State Pair Rule
rules.body: Red and green mean outcome and nothing else, and they never travel alone. The verdict is a filled disc with a check or cross plus a word; chosen options carry a check or cross glyph; a missed correct option is labelled Correct answer.

rules.name: The One Data Hue Rule
rules.body: Charts use Data Blue for measured values, Line Strong for values below a threshold and Ledger Green only for good. No other chart hues.

rules.name: The Mono Evidence Rule
rules.body: Anything a person may need to read character by character is set in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono: question and activity codes, employee IDs, resume codes, addresses and URLs quoted in prompts, the countdown, numbered keyboard hints.

rules.name: The Weight Ladder Rule
rules.body: One family; hierarchy comes from weight and size: 800 for headings and the wordmark, 700 for titles and statuses, 600 for labels and buttons, 400 for reading. No second display face.

rules.name: The Title-First Rule
rules.body: A heading stands at the top of its block. Codes, statuses and counts sit in a meta row beneath it; nothing sits above it as a kicker. Uppercase tracked lettering belongs to the exhibit tag alone.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Numbers that get compared (tables, times, scores, counts, chart ticks) use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Two Shadows Rule
rules.body: Only the plate and things that float get shadows. Panels, option rows, notes and cards separate from the ground by tone and a 1px ring.

rules.name: The Keyline Rule
rules.body: Anything drawn on top of a screenshot carries its own graphite keyline or halo, because the evidence underneath can be any colour.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Brand blue means act here or you are here: the filled button, the selected pill or radio card, the active tab, the card being edited. Each region carries at most one filled button (New activity on the list, Share in the activity header, Publish results in its message bar, Save in the save bar, the confirm button in a dialog); everything else is outline or ghost.

rules.name: The Status Pair Rule (console)
rules.body: Green, amber and red mark status and answers, never decoration, and never alone: badges carry a dot and a word, correct answers a check, wrong ones a cross and a word, the autosave state an icon and a sentence.

rules.name: The Re-point Rule
rules.body: Console code names the console tokens (brand, ok, bad, warn, the neutrals) or a shared token that `.admin-ui` re-points. It reaches for marker, manila, ledger green or evidence red only for marks drawn on a screenshot.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Semibold (600) carries every heading, label, button and emphasis; regular (400) carries reading. The Evidence Room's 700 and 800 ladder does not apply in the console.

rules.name: The Plain Words Rule
rules.body: The console shows people's words, not the system's. Questions are numbered 1, 2, 3 straight through the activity, in the builder, the summary, the drawer and the red-flag map; sections are Section 1, Section 2; statuses read Draft, Scheduled, Open and Closed. No question codes, exhibit letters, CASE numbers or code chips, and mono only for strings a person types.

rules.name: The No Sideways Page Rule
rules.body: A console page never scrolls horizontally. Lists stack below 640px with the ⋯ menu visible; grid columns are `minmax(0, 1fr)` (the Responses page, the question list, answer previews, bar rows, the red-flag map); flex children carry `min-w-0` and titles truncate or clamp; header actions, filters, message-bar actions and setting rows wrap, a setting's control dropping beneath its label. A table wider than the screen scrolls inside its own card, never the page.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Building and settings are one centred column (800px and 760px), like a form. No outline pane, side preview or second column; Preview is a dialog.

rules.name: The Lift Rule
rules.body: Cards rest on the card shadow and floating layers on pop; nothing else casts a shadow except the save bar and the switch thumb. Only a collapsed question card lifts on hover.

dos: **Do** give each view one marker-yellow action (#f2c230 with #1a1c1e text): New activity, Continue on entry, Check answer, Submit answers, View certificate. Moving on (Next, Continue, Finish) is the graphite ink button.
**Do** set codes, employee IDs, resume codes and quoted addresses in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono, and compared numbers in tabular numerals.
**Do** put evidence on the white plate with the plate shadow, zoom controls and the full-screen viewer, and collapse it to the 144px tap strip on phones until the reveal.
**Do** reveal red flags as numbered tent markers on the evidence with a matching numbered evidence log, linked by hover in both directions.
**Do** pair red and green with a glyph and a word: the verdict disc with a check or cross, plus Correct or Not quite.
**Do** keep text at Ink 3 (#5f676c) or darker on light surfaces and Shell Muted (#a9afb2) or lighter on graphite.
**Do** keep employee touch targets at 44px or more: option rows 48px, primary buttons lg (44px) or xl (48px), review cells 44px, rating squares 48px.
**Do** separate surfaces by tone and 1px hairlines: white panels with a 1px Line ring on the concrete ground.
**Do** use the 2px graphite focus outline with a 2px offset on light surfaces, and mark graphite regions `.on-shell` so focus turns marker yellow.
**Do** keep reveal motion on ease-out-expo with the 90ms stagger, and let the global reduced-motion clamp land every animation on its final frame.
**Do** give each console region one filled Brand Blue button (#0f6cbd, white text): New activity, Share, Publish results, Save, Open now; everything else is outline or ghost.
**Do** put console content in white 8px cards on the card shadow over the #f5f5f5 ground, with no card borders.
**Do** keep building and settings in one centred column (800px Questions, 760px Settings) and list pages at 1120px.
**Do** number questions 1, 2, 3 straight through the activity, call sections Section 1, Section 2, and show status as Draft, Scheduled, Open and Closed badges with a dot.
**Do** keep "Publish" for results only: activities are opened (Open now, Schedule), closed (Close now, Reopen) and taken back to draft.
**Do** state where results stand in a message bar at the top of Responses, and confirm Publish results and Hide results in a dialog.
**Do** pair console status colour with a word or glyph: badge dot and word, a check and Correct, a cross and Wrong, a check on the correct answer's bar.
**Do** draw the correct answer's bar in Ok green with a check and every other bar in Brand Blue; score columns below the pass mark are Admin Line Strong.
**Do** turn console lists into stacked rows below 640px with the ⋯ menu visible, and give grid columns `minmax(0, 1fr)` so no page scrolls sideways.
**Do** lay settings out as rows, label and hint on the left and the control on the right, and show the save bar only while something is unsaved.
**Do** set console page titles and stat values at 28px semibold (36px line), body at 14px, and every emphasis at 600.
donts: **Don't** use marker yellow as a panel background, as decoration, or as text on a light surface, where it is 1.7:1.
**Don't** use manila for actions, or red and green for anything except outcome state and errors.
**Don't** put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading; meta (code chip, status, counts) goes beneath the title.
**Don't** use gradients, glass panels or decorative blur. The only blur is a small legibility blur behind 95%-opaque sticky controls.
**Don't** use side-stripe or left-border callouts; notes are full washes or ringed white cards, and quoted messages are fully bordered boxes.
**Don't** round surfaces past 2px or chart data ends past 4px, and don't use pills except for dots, radio indicators and the switch.
**Don't** add chart hues beyond Data Blue, Line Strong and Ledger Green; the leftover --chart-2 to --chart-5 variables are not part of the system.
**Don't** use the stock shadcn Badge, Tabs, Checkbox or chart tooltip as shipped; they still carry pill and soft-shadow defaults. Use StatusBadge, CodeChip, the workspace tab bar and the option row.
**Don't** build the category default: a centred quiz card, a percentage progress bar, confetti, or a blue SaaS shell.
**Don't** render phishing evidence as live HTML or invent an HRRL logo; evidence is an image on the plate and the brand is the type wordmark.

**Don't** bring Evidence Room furniture into the console chrome: no graphite rail, marker-yellow buttons, manila tags, exhibit letters, CASE codes, S1·Q01 code chips or tent markers outside the red-flag map and the Preview.
**Don't** use Microsoft logos, product names or trademarks in the console, or a stand-in logo; the product name is set in type.
**Don't** add a second column, outline pane or side preview to the builder; Preview is a dialog.
**Don't** use Brand Blue for anything but the app bar, actions, selection, the active tab, links, focus and chart data; never as a panel fill or heading colour.
**Don't** use green, amber or red in the console without a word or glyph, or for anything but status, answers and errors.
**Don't** let a console page scroll sideways, or hide the row menu on phones.
**Don't** border console cards, or add shadows beyond card, card hover, pop and the save bar.
**Don't** set console text in mono except strings people type (passwords, ID patterns, number answers).

worlds.name: Admin Console
worlds.overview:
The console is a sibling of the tools the CISO office already works in all day: Outlook, Teams and Microsoft Forms. An admin builds an activity the way they build a form (a title card, one column of numbered question cards, Add new question), shares a link, reads Responses as a summary of simple bars, and presses Publish results when ready. Nothing in it should need learning; the familiarity is the design.

It is Fluent-style and quiet: white cards on a soft two-layer shadow over a light grey page, a 48px brand-blue app bar carrying the product name, Segoe UI Variable at a 14px base, 4px controls and 8px cards. Brand blue marks the primary action, the current selection and the active tab; green, amber and red mark status and always travel with a word or a glyph. The words are plain: no internal codes, exhibit tags or code chips. The Evidence Room appears inside the console only where an employee's view is the subject, in the Preview dialog and the red-flag map.

It refuses the previous admin look (dark graphite rail, yellow buttons, CASE codes and S1·Q01 chips, manila tags, the three-pane builder), and it borrows Microsoft's design language only, never a Microsoft logo, product name or trademark.
keyCharacteristics: Brand-blue app bar, light grey page, white cards.
One centred column for building (800px) and settings (760px); lists at 1120px.
Brand blue for the primary action, selection, the active tab, links and chart data only.
Green, amber and red for status, always with a dot, check, cross or word.
Segoe UI Variable at 14px; semibold carries all emphasis; 28px is the top step.
4px controls, 8px cards, fully round pills and badges.
Lists become stacked rows on phones; no page scrolls sideways.
